source_record.name: Secomber
source_record.summary: Small walled town on three stone hills on the north bank of the River Delimbiyr, where the Unicorn Run joins it; a stop on the Delimbiyr Route (Daggerford to the west, Zelbross and Loudwater to the east) with the Secomber Trail running north to Uluvin; farming, fishing, stone-cutting and caravan trade; hobgoblin tribute by 1479 DR.

identity.subregion: North bank of the River Delimbiyr at the mouth of the Unicorn Run; High Moor to the south
identity.ruler_office: Lord (14th century DR); no ruler recorded for the late 15th century

periods.note: Nothing is verified for 1492 DR itself.

engine_record.population_note: Gazetteer estimate with no reference year. Sourced figures: 900 (1358 and 1367 DR) and 1,417 (1372 DR) (SE4).

area_geography.summary: Town on three stone hills north of the Delimbiyr; the Unicorn Run flows south along the east side to join the river; the Delimbiyr Route runs along the north bank from Daggerford (west) over the Unicorn Run to Zelbross and Loudwater (east); the Secomber Trail leaves the Route north to Uluvin; the High Moor lies south of the river.
routes: Delimbiyr Route (west to Daggerford and the Trade Way; east to Zelbross and Loudwater)
area_geography.orientation: North up, as drawn by the compass on the reference town maps; not confirmed by a written source.
sources: The North: Guide to the Savage Frontier (1996), pp. 63, 76 and Map of Interior

town_plan.source: Three-hill town map of Secomber (wiki file Secomber.jpg, 4th-edition era, caption 1479 DR; publication not identified), stored in this folder as three copies of different resolution and colour
town_plan.stored_note: The README says published images are linked, not stored; these files were added to the folder as reference images on 2026-10-15 and their provenance is not recorded. caa1e0862716ef40c7b66b7c3409eff2.png is the parchment version; 9966bc80353646297704ac0f85c03cc0.png is a green-wash version and OIP.webp a small copy; all show the same plan.
town_plan.orientation: Compass rose at the west side, north up
layout: Three ring-shaped hills, each with houses on concentric rings, enclosed together by a wall that runs from the south side of the town round the north and east sides
A palisaded fort stands on the south-west hill
A pool and a cluster of larger buildings (inns and halls) lie in the middle, where the three hills meet
A road runs from the centre south-east to the junction on the Delimbiyr Route; a second road runs south-west to the Route
The Delimbiyr Route runs east to west along the river; the Secomber Trail leaves it at the junction and runs north to Uluvin
A wooden bridge carries the Route over the Unicorn Run to the east, towards Loudwater
A strip of buildings and about nine piers line the north bank of the Delimbiyr, with a few more buildings at the junction
A planted field lies in the north-west corner

other_reference_images.kind: Digital map with nine numbered sites, a wide Delimbiyr and bridges to the south bank; no legend
other_reference_images.note: Layout differs from the three-hill plan; not used.

evidence.finding: Town on three stone hills, north of the Delimbiyr at the Unicorn Run confluence
Settled in 516 DR by halflings of Delimbiyr Vale and humans of Delimbiyran
Humans form a majority or about half; halflings almost as numerous, with small dwarf, gnome and moon elf populations
Delimbiyr River runs west along south; Unicorn Run flows south along east and joins it
High Moor is south of river
Delimbiyr Route follows river, toward Trade Way/Daggerford to west and Zelbross/Loudwater east
Trail north-west toward Uluvin
Farming, fishing, stone-cutting and caravan guide/guard services
Hobgoblin raids and tribute by 1479 DR; impoverishment noted by circa 1491 DR
900 residents
900 residents
1,417 residents
1,300 residents in engine; date/evidence not supplied
Six to nine elected Rods of Justice and nine-landowner juries described in later publication
About 30 Lords Alliance soldiers and over 100 militia recorded in older sources
Samril’s Fine Blades finishes blades for shipment to Waterdeep
Gleskur’s Finemetals produces braided copper wire
Singing Sprite inn, recorded 1367 and 1396 DR
Seven-Stringed Harp tavern
Halfling vineyards northwest of town produce sour vinegar
Moon Mountain Brewery, roughly two days north, supplied ale; Moon Rum available in Secomber
